source_name: Banka Slovenije – Seznam notifikacij plačilnih institucij (PSD2 passporting notifications, PDF catalogue)
why_relevant: Lists foreign payment institutions notified to operate in Slovenia — the inbound-competition view that no domestic filing register captures. Directly relevant to sizing the payments market and spotting new entrants.

Capital markets days carry the multi-year strategy, mid-term targets and technology/digital roadmap in far more depth than quarterly decks. NLB's 2026 event was staged in Sarajevo, signalling SEE-expansion framing.

source_name: ATVP - Poročanje v enotni elektronski obliki (ESEF reporting)
why_relevant: Defines the machine-readable (iXBRL/ESEF) format in which Slovenian issuers must file annual financial reports - directly determines whether annual reports can be parsed structurally rather than as PDFs.

source_name: Bankart annual reports (Letno poročilo) PDF archive on wp-content
why_relevant: Audited annual reports carry transaction volumes, card counts, market shares, ownership by member banks and investment plans — the hardest quantitative baseline available for Slovenian card processing.

source_name: Bankart public payment-system rulebooks (Javni dokument za PS / Opis plačilnih sistemov)
why_relevant: Mandatory public disclosure documents describing BIPS, SIMP-PS and card settlement — participants, settlement cycles, risk framework. These are the authoritative technical description of Slovenian clearing and change with each scheme release.

source_name: LJSE INFO HRAMBA – officially appointed mechanism (OAM) for storing regulated information
why_relevant: The storage mechanism behind SEOnet: defines how regulated information is captured and archived and how third parties access it. Reading the rules tells a collector what the guaranteed retention, format and metadata are — and whether the OAM, not SEOnet, is the better long-term archive endpoint.

source_name: STA / STAkrog – event and conference coverage of banking gatherings
why_relevant: The Slovenian Press Agency reports on Dan slovenskih bančnikov and ZBS conferences, frequently quoting statements from the stage. Where the organiser posts no proceedings, agency and newspaper coverage (STA, Delo, Gorenjski glas, Večer) is the de facto archive.

source_name: Halcom bank terms & conditions PDFs (Splošni pogoji Hal E-Bank)
why_relevant: Dated, versioned contractual documents in the vendor's uploads directory. They carry effective dates and market scope, and the uploads path (/app/uploads/YYYY/MM/) is itself a harvestable timeline of vendor document releases per market.

source_name: WEBSI – Digitalni presežki Slovenije (national digital project awards) shortlists
why_relevant: Slovenia's main digital-project awards (14th edition 2025, record 225 entries; Mastercard Slovenija among winners). Entries are self-declared achievement disclosures by banks, card schemes and their agencies — naming the project, the client, the agency and often the technology. Shortlists reveal digital initiatives never covered in financial reporting.

source_name: Bank-hosted Hal E-Bank manuals (e.g. UniCredit Bank Slovenija)
why_relevant: A bank publishing a Halcom-branded manual on its own domain is hard confirmation that the bank runs that vendor's product. Searching bank domains for vendor product names is a reliable technique for confirming vendor-bank pairings without any procurement record.

source_name: EBAday (Euro Banking Association / Finextra) – speaker lineups
why_relevant: Europe's main payments-practitioner conference; published speaker lineups (100+ experts, 2026 edition Copenhagen, 16-17 June) are a searchable register in which any Slovenian bank or processor participation surfaces with title and affiliation. Finextra reliably publishes the full list in article form, which is easier to parse than the event site.

source_name: Moje finance – 'Naj banka' / najugodnejša banka annual awards
why_relevant: Consumer-finance magazine's methodology-based annual bank rankings (deposits, bank packages, consumer loans). Banks publish the results themselves as achievement disclosures, and the category structure reveals competitive pricing positioning. Award pages on bank sites are dated and durable.
SEE-focused wire that reliably summarises paywalled Moody's/S&P/Fitch actions on Slovenian banks in English within hours — the practical substitute when agency PDFs are inaccessible.

entity_name: COBISS+ bibliographic record for Bančni vestnik
source_name: COBISS+ bibliographic record for Bančni vestnik
why_relevant: Slovenian union catalogue record gives authoritative bibliographic metadata (ISSN 0005-4631, publisher, run since 1952) and locates physical/library access to gated issues — a legitimate route around the paywall.

source_name: Mestna občina Ljubljana / MojaObčina.si – municipal payment-service announcements
why_relevant: Municipalities are large payment-accepting entities and publish dated notices when a new payment channel goes live (parking apps, transport, utility counters). MojaObčina.si aggregates the same notices across many municipalities, making it an efficient way to detect acceptance changes in smaller towns that never reach national media.

source_name: Morningstar DBRS – Republic of Slovenia rating research
why_relevant: Fourth ECAI covering Slovenia; DBRS press releases are generally openly readable and include banking-sector commentary within sovereign rationale.

source_name: Raiffeisen Research – CEE Banking Sector Report (annual, Slovenia included)
why_relevant: Bank-analyst (sell-side) annual benchmark of CEE banking markets that names Slovenia in specifics such as banking-sector taxation and cross-border market share — a forward-looking view distinct from supervisory data.

source_name: The Fintech Times — Slovenia market feature
why_relevant: UK fintech trade press occasionally produces English market overviews of Slovenia (digital adoption rates, regulatory alignment with the EU digital finance agenda, local fintech actors), which are useful for actor-map expansion even though they are secondary analysis.

source_name: ZBS YouTube channel – recorded conference sessions
why_relevant: ZBS publishes video recordings of its banking conference sessions (e.g. 'Bančna konferenca, dopoldanski del'). Video is often the ONLY archive of what executives actually said, since slide decks are rarely posted. Transcribable into a durable text record.
